Retrieved via Exa search highlights (Reuters newswire text + CNBC + The National). Direct quotes/figures below.

DEFINITIVE FRIDAY 17 JULY 2026 CLOSE:
- Reuters (New York, July 17): "Brent crude futures settled $3.87, or 4.59%, higher to $88.10 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures rose $3.54, or 4.48%, at $82.49. Both were at their highest since mid-June."
- CNBC: "Brent crude futures... advanced about 4.6% to close at $88.10 per barrel. Meanwhile, U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures gained about 4.5% to settle at $82.49."
- The National: "Brent... jumped 4.59 per cent to settle at $88.10 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate... added 4.42 per cent to close at $82.44." Both settled above $80 for the first time in a month.
- WEEKLY: both benchmarks gained about 16% for the week — strongest weekly gain since April (Reuters/The National). Brent's third consecutive weekly gain.
- SHIPPING (Kpler, via The National): confirmed crude and condensate transit through the Strait of Hormuz fell 62% to 4.1 million barrels per day; regional loadings dropped 47%.
- Iran pressed the Houthis to be ready to close the Red Sea (Bab el-Mandeb) route if the US attacks Iran's power infrastructure — raising prospect of a second chokepoint (Reuters).
- IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol warned global energy security remains fragile.
- Context: ~20% of global oil supplies normally flow through the Strait of Hormuz.

Earlier cache figure (Trading Economics, ~85.95 on 17 July intraday) superseded by the confirmed settle of $88.10.
